equity_bridge.item: Investment securities portfolio (listed at fair value less tax on unrealised gain, unlisted at book)
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 yuho: listed その他有価証券 fair value 33,879m at 31 Mar 2026 (unrealised gain reserve 14,234m after tax => ~20.5bn pre-tax gain; ~6.3bn tax if sold => ~27,600m realisable) + unquoted equities 6,736m at book. Dividend income (986m) is stripped from the flows to match. In Q1 FY2027 the company sold holdings for a 2,510m gain, converting part of this to cash after the balance-sheet date -- consistent with the March basis used for both cash and securities.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: blend: FY2027 guidance (+6.2%), 2030 Vision (800bn by FY2031 = 4.9% CAGR), equity 5yr CAGR 4.1% (understated by a 50-70% payout ratio) and revenue 3yr CAGR 3.8%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 3yr CAGR of 25% diverges from equity (5.4%) and revenue (3.8%) because FY2023 EPS (158.71) was a trough year with 7.5% EBITDA margin; the 5yr EPS CAGR of 5.9% is the representative figure. Owner-FCF CAGRs (-19% 3yr, +18% 5yr) are meaningless: FY2023 OCF of 61.8bn and FY2021 OCF of 25.5bn are working-capital swings, which is why the model is built from components rather than an FCF trend.
historical_growth.notes: CAGR bases: revenue FY2021 563,252 / FY2023 563,295 -> FY2026 630,658; diluted EPS FY2021 232.21 / FY2023 158.71 -> FY2026 309.71; equity FY2021 327,554 / FY2023 341,094 -> FY2026 399,894; owner FCF FY2021 ~12,310 / FY2023 ~52,000 -> FY2026 27,639 (reported less SBC less interest+dividends received). SBC is ~0.02-0.04% of revenue across the whole history so the owner-FCF adjustment does not alter the growth picture; the interest+dividend strip is ~1bn/yr.

scenario_narratives.base: COMSYS executes roughly on its 2030 Vision but not above it: FY2027 guidance (670bn revenue, 54bn OP) is met on strong Q1 orders (+13.2%), growth decelerates from 6% toward 2% as the mobile quality programme fades and data-centre and social-infrastructure work replace it. EBITDA margin eases from a 9.9% peak to 9.5% as acquired social-systems subsidiaries dilute the mix, consistent with the plan's own ~7.5% OP target on 800bn. Working capital keeps absorbing ~20% of revenue growth, so owner FCF runs at 4-5% of revenue -- around 26-40bn a year -- while ~70% of profit is returned as dividends and buybacks. Terminal value is bound by the 15x owner-FCF cap, not Gordon growth.
scenario_narratives.bull: Data-centre buildout plus NTT's IOWN fixed-network rebuild and continued mobile densification keep order intake growing 7%+ for three years; the 800bn revenue target is reached a year early and margins expand to ~10.8% on productivity gains and scale in social systems. Working-capital intensity falls as large projects carry advance payments. Terminal 17x reflects a re-rating toward a diversified infrastructure-services multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: The NTT group, 26% of revenue directly (NTT East 15.9%, NTT West 10.5%) and ~45% via the telecom-carrier segment, cuts capex after the mobile quality programme; revenue shrinks in FY2029-30, margins fall to 8% on labour inflation, and the stock de-rates to 12x. Net cash and the securities portfolio limit the downside -- they are ~600 JPY/share of value before any operating cash flow.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A net-cash, low-growth Japanese infrastructure contractor valued on normalised owner free cash flow built from components, because single-year FCF is dominated by receivables timing. The value is roughly half operating cash flows over ten years, a third terminal value capped at 15x FCF, and ~600 JPY/share of net cash, cross-shareholdings and securities. SBC is immaterial, so house and street bases coincide. Risk from NTT concentration and the Japanese construction cycle is charged in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, not in the discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: NTT group capex cycle: NTT East/West 26.4% of revenue directly; the docomo mobile quality-improvement programme that drove FY2026-27 growth is finite.
Working-capital intensity: ~20-27% of revenue tied up in receivables and contract WIP; a 10pp change in the capture assumption moves owner FCF by ~4bn/yr on 6% growth.
Terminal multiple: Gordon at 1.5% exceeds the 15x cap in base and bull, so the cap is load-bearing; a 12x cap (bear) removes ~700 JPY/share.
Construction-labour shortage and 2024 overtime caps: cost inflation not fully recoverable under NTT unit-price contracts.
Margin mean reversion: FY2026 EBITDA margin of 9.85% is a seven-year high; the FY2020-26 average is 8.9% and the 2030 Vision implies ~9.3%.

Unmodelled debt-like items: net retirement-benefit liability ~12bn (~103 JPY/share) and asset-retirement/environmental provisions; and the securities bridge assumes listed holdings are realisable at fair value less tax.
Price anchor: regular-session intraday print; balance sheet is 31 Mar 2026 by design (seasonality) with the 30 Jun 2026 net cash of 68.5bn recorded in net_debt_note.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 118,000,000 issued less 2,859,056 treasury shares (incl. ESOP-trust holdings) at 30 Jun 2026 = 115.14m, plus ~1.18m dilutive shares implied by Q1 FY2027 basic/diluted EPS of 73.89/73.14 (stock acquisition rights, 1,024m JPY carrying value). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the ~10bn JPY/yr buyback pace (FY2026 10,046m; a further 655k shares bought May-Jun 2026) more than funds the flat count.
inputs.net_debt_note: Year-end (31 Mar 2026) balance sheet used deliberately rather than the later 30 Jun 2026 one. COMSYS's working capital is strongly seasonal: receivables peak at the March fiscal year-end (209.9bn) and are collected in Q1 (151.1bn at June), so June cash (71,262m, net cash 68,486m) is a seasonal high that reverses by the 9-month mark every year in the history (short-term debt rises to 24-36bn at 9M). Using the June figure would add ~255 JPY/share of value that is working-capital timing, not surplus cash. total_debt = short-term borrowings 2,413m + current portion of long-term 13m; bonds nil; finance-lease liabilities (1,017m) excluded under lease treatment (B). cash = cash & equivalents per the cash-flow statement (balance-sheet 現金預金 42,033m includes 700m of longer-dated deposits).
inputs.interest_income_note: 1,063m is the cash-flow statement line 利息及び配当金の受取額 (interest AND dividends received, FY2026: dividends 986m + interest 76m). Both are stripped from owner FCF because both source assets are added back in the equity bridge (cash in net_debt; the investment-securities portfolio as an equity_bridge item). Matching-asset rule, owner-fcf-adaptations section (d).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 yuho (有価証券報告書 filed 2026-06-22), SG&A note: 株式報酬費用 148m JPY (FY2025: 187m). Restricted-stock plan for directors; no equity-award tax withholding line exists (EquityAwardTaxes = 0). SBC is ~0.02% of revenue: SBC-zero-market conditions apply and the house/street band is degenerate (~10-20 JPY/share wide) -- band_position is not a meaningful reading for this ticker.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-26T00:18:51Z (09:18 JST, regular session intraday print on the TSE Prime market; Yahoo Finance chart API)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the flows: 10-year JGB ~1.7% (Oct 2026) + Japan ERP 6.0% x beta ~1.0 = 7.7%, rounded to 8.0% as an effectively all-equity rate (borrowings are 0.4% of EV, so WACC = cost of equity). Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality and NTT-concentration risk are charged ONCE, in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked into the discount rate (adaptations section (f)). The house ~9% JPY keiretsu reference is for levered auto-parts suppliers with one OEM customer and negative net cash swings; COMSYS is net cash with a 70% payout, so 8% sits between that and a pure low-beta utility-like rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. J-GAAP filer: operating leases are already expensed inside EBITDA. Finance leases are immaterial (liabilities 410m current + 607m non-current = 1,017m at 31 Mar 2026; principal repaid 518m in FY2026) and are charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path = 0.08% of revenue, with the liabilities EXCLUDED from total_debt. Not charged twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows; non-controlling interests (6,520m book at 31 Mar 2026; NCI share of profit ~0.5-0.7bn/yr, i.e. <2% of group profit) deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at book value. FY0 tie: modelled NOPAT 50,904 x (1-0.306) = 35,327m vs attributable net income 36,307m -- the gap is non-operating income (dividends 986m, rent, securities gains 914m) less NCI, i.e. within non-operating noise.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'), with the owner-fcf-adaptations applied: JPY-built WACC, lease treatment (B), NCI charged once in the bridge, excluded dividend/interest income matched by the securities portfolio and cash in the bridge, SBC-zero-market handling. Not a REIT, bank or holdco: COMSYS is a pure-play Japanese telecom/ICT/social-infrastructure construction contractor (telecom carrier ~45% of revenue, IT solutions ~20%, social systems ~35%), 100% Japan, 23 years listed, J-GAAP consolidated. FIRST VALUATION (no prior DCF, no MEMORY entry). FCF BASE: the parser's warning is correct -- reported OCF swings 5bn to 62bn on receivables timing (FY2019 and FY2022 FCF negative), so the valuation is NOT anchored on any single year's FCF. It is built from components calibrated to FY2026 actuals and the FY2027 guidance (EBITDA 9.85% -> 9.95% guide-implied; D&A 1.75%; capex 2.1% = FY2022-26 average of 2.1%; cash tax 30.6% statutory vs 32.7% paid in FY2026), with working capital modelled as a cash DRAIN on growth (wc_capture -20%: year-end net operating WC is ~27% of revenue, ~20% on a through-the-year average). Cross-check: 7-year (FY2020-26) average reported FCF is 21.1bn/yr (3.6% margin) against year-1 modelled owner FCF of ~26bn (3.9%) on a higher margin base -- consistent. HORIZON: 10 years so that the 2030 Vision period (to FY2031) is explicit and growth has decelerated to Japanese nominal trend before capitalising. TERMINAL: Gordon at 1.5% vs a 15x owner-FCF cap for a cyclical contractor; expect the cap to bind in base/bull. QUALITATIVE SOURCE: drivers were set from the FY2026 yuho and Q1 FY2027 tanshin directly; 1721.T_Analysis.json landed afterwards and was checked before shipping -- it corroborates NTT East+West ~26% of revenue, a ~320bn backlog (+20% YoY), the 11bn buyback authorisation to Mar 2027 and the 135 JPY FY2027 dividend, and moved no driver path. PENSION: net retirement-benefit liability 11,991m (~103 JPY/share) is NOT deducted -- service cost is inside EBITDA and cash contributions run through OCF; noted as a modest unmodelled debt-like item. PRICE: intraday regular-session print; replace at the next close if volatile.

bear.narrative: NTT capex downcycle: the docomo mobile quality-improvement surge ends after FY2027 and NTT East/West fixed-line capex continues its secular decline (copper retirement, FTTH saturation); NCC (KDDI/SoftBank/Rakuten) capex stays depressed. Revenue falls 2% a year in FY2029-30 while construction-labour cost inflation and the 2024 overtime caps cannot be fully passed through, compressing EBITDA to 8.0% (below the FY2023 trough of 7.5% only briefly avoided). Receivable terms lengthen (WC drain 25% of growth, cash released in down years). Terminal multiple 12x, the low end for a sub-scale, single-country contractor.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 = FY2027 company guidance (670bn, +6.2%, reaffirmed 14 Aug 2026 with Q1 orders +13.2%). Years 2-5 decelerate 5.0 -> 3.5% to land at ~790bn in FY2031, marginally below the 2030 Vision's 800bn target (which includes bolt-on M&A). Then glide to 2.0%, Japan nominal trend.
base.margin_rationale: Year 1 9.95% EBITDA reproduces guided OP of 54bn after D&A/lease/SBC (model EBIT ~54.2bn). Mild reversion to 9.5% from year 6: the FY2026 margin (9.85%) is a 7-year high lifted by NTT docomo mobile quality-improvement work that management describes as a multi-year but finite programme; the 2030 Vision itself implies ~7.5% OP (~9.3% EBITDA) on 800bn, i.e. the plan assumes margin dilution from social-systems M&A. 9.5% sits between the plan and the FY2024-26 run-rate.
base.wc_rationale: Negative capture: a contractor with receivables + contract WIP (~255bn) far above payables + advances (~90bn). Each yen of revenue growth ties up ~20 sen of working capital; this is the mechanism behind the volatile reported OCF and it must be charged.
base.capex_rationale: 2.1% = FY2022-FY2026 average (62,330m on 2,968,771m revenue), spanning the FY2024 3.3% peak and the FY2025 1.7% trough. D&A 1.75% matches FY2026 (1.77%) and Q1 FY2027 annualised (1.74%); capex > D&A reflects data-centre/construction-equipment investment and acquisitions of small subsidiaries.

bull.narrative: 2030 Vision beaten: revenue passes 800bn in FY2030 on the data-centre construction wave, NTT's IOWN/all-photonics fixed-network rebuild and mobile quality programme, and social-systems (renewables, grid storage, water, pole-free) scaling with acquired subsidiaries. Productivity (BIM/CIM, prefabrication, multi-skilling) lifts EBITDA to ~10.8%; advance payments on large DC projects ease working-capital drag to 15% of growth.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% for single-customer-group dependency: NTT East and NTT West alone are 26.4% of FY2026 revenue (yuho major-customer table), and the telecom-carrier segment, almost entirely NTT group and three NCCs, is ~45% -- the company's own risk section says this concentration 'is expected to continue for the foreseeable future'. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things (DC boom sustained, NTT IOWN capex, margin expansion against a labour shortage) to go right at once. Base 50%: the FY2027 guide is conservative relative to Q1 (NI +47%) and management has beaten its own targets in FY2026.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
